title: Muse has a voice mode now
snippet: Meta now lets you have voice conversations with your Muse AI agent in real time, CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced today. As you chat with your Muse agent, the avatar at the top of your conversation animates in time with the words that it's saying. title: Google's Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash stretches AI video clips to 15 seconds and cuts pricing by 30 percent
snippet: Google Deepmind is making Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available. The video-generation model now creates clips up to 15 seconds long, can be edited step by step via conversation, and costs just $0.07 per second at 720p, 30 percent less than its predecessor. Users who draft in low resolution and upscale only the final result can save even more. title: SuperAlloy enters semiconductor pilot production in 3Q26
snippet: SuperAlloy reported strong third-quarter 2026 results, with consolidated revenue rising 18.5% year-over-year to NT$2.016 billion (US$61.4 million) as demand from international supercar and luxury vehicle brands increased. title: Apple's OLED shift challenges Radiant, but foldable iPhone offers a way forward
snippet: Apple's growing adoption of OLED displays is reshaping its supply chain, prompting key supplier Radiant Opto-Electronics to expand beyond conventional backlight modules into advanced optical technologies. The Taiwanese company is strengthening its partnership with Apple through several new products, including a solution designed to reduce the visible display crease in Apple's first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo.

title: DIGITIMES Insight: Foxconn extends AI strategy to data center system integration, targeting modular computing delivery with DSX POD
snippet: At Hon Hai Tech Day 2026 (HHTD 26), Foxconn showcased the Nvidia DSX POD containerized solution. By leveraging factory pre-building, electromechanical integration, and pre-testing, Foxconn integrates computing racks, networking equipment, power distribution, and liquid cooling systems into rapidly deployable computing units. This approach assists Nvidia in transforming its AI computing platform into a modular data center architecture capable of mass production and on-site delivery.

title: Google Plans to Spend $17 Billion on Wyoming Data Center
snippet: Alphabet Inc.’s Google will spend $17 billion to build a data center in Wyoming, formally putting a price tag on the proposal two days after voters across the US delivered a broad rebuke to the development of such massive projects for artificial intelligence work.

title: Defense Tech Boom Fuels Shield AI’s Expansion
snippet: Shield AI is acquiring counter-drone technology company Echodyne in a deal worth more than $5 billion, a major expansion of its push into next-generation defense technology. CEO Gary Steele discusses why counter-drone capabilities are becoming increasingly critical and why investor appetite for defense tech remains strong as Shield AI raises new capital at a sharply higher valuation. He joins Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Agility Robotics Makes Public Debut as Humanoids Scale
snippet: Agility Robotics is making its public market debut, becoming the first dedicated US humanoid robotics company to go public. CEO Peggy Johnson discusses growing deployments of its Digit robot, $300 million in pending orders and why the company chose to go public now despite market volatility. She joins Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Apple Taps Bond Market for $7B as Tech Sells Off
snippet: Apple is looking to raise about $7 billion in its first investment-grade bond sale in more than a year, with proceeds helping to fund share buybacks. Bloomberg Intelligence’s Robert Schiffman says the move looks opportunistic rather than driven by a need for cash. He also explains why Apple is standing out in the broader tech selloff as investors reassess the debt and spending behind the AI infrastructure boom. He joins Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Could Political Pushback on Data Centers Drive Financial Discipline?
snippet: As tech markets tumble, Anna Rathbun, founder and CEO of Grenadilla Advisory, sees a buying opportunity in less-levered AI-related firms. She says new oversight and regulations from a Democratic-controlled Congress could bring some financial discipline to the data center buildout. Rathbun joins Tim Stenovec on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: China’s ‘Lipstick King’ hawks tokens as AI gets mass-market Singles’ Day push
snippet: China’s “Lipstick King” has traded make-up swatches for artificial intelligence. Top live-streamer Li Jiaqi on Monday evening teamed up with an executive from Alibaba Group Holding to pitch AI subscriptions, selling nearly 100,000 monthly packages in just 30 minutes, according to data provided by the e-commerce giant. The broadcast on Taobao and Tmall – Alibaba’s largest domestic online marketplace – marked the first time generative AI products have taken centre stage during the annual Singles’.
